title: Regulated payment platform transition: operational-handover
summary: A payment platform across two jurisdictions, legacy ledger migration, external settlement and 24-hour incident response. Preserve reconciled balances and a 15-minute recovery objective while retaining auditable transaction evidence within approved jurisdictions. A staged migration uses immutable event IDs, dual reconciliation and approved regional failover; outbound settlement remains gated by ledger equality.

scenario.name: Regulated payment platform transition
scenario.scope: A payment platform across two jurisdictions, legacy ledger migration, external settlement and 24-hour incident response.
scenario.drivers: Preserve reconciled balances and a 15-minute recovery objective while retaining auditable transaction evidence within approved jurisdictions.
scenario.design: A staged migration uses immutable event IDs, dual reconciliation and approved regional failover; outbound settlement remains gated by ledger equality.
scenario.cost: EUR 8400000 transition and EUR 1900000 annual operation; five-year benefits EUR 16000000, sensitive to delay and compliance cost by 35 percent.
scenario.risk: Cross-border failover can violate approved data-location constraints; regional routing and policy checks reduce exposure, with legal interpretation remaining reviewable.
scenario.operations: The payment service owner authorises cutover; independent control assurance and round-the-clock operations review reconciliation before traffic migration.

readiness_evidence.criterion: Repeated event IDs must not create a second ledger entry

privacy_analysis.description: Transaction identifiers are pseudonymised; access is role-limited, retention is tied to the approved purpose and deletion is verified in rehearsal.

regulatory_analysis.description: Data-location and transaction-retention obligations require competent jurisdictional interpretation; the fixture does not assert a legal exemption or real compliance approval.

evidence.description: Scenario assumptions and fabricated rehearsal observations for test development only; not real customer evidence.
